learning_outcomes.text: Students will have extended knowledge in materials engineering, understand the fundamental physical-chemical properties of metals, ceramics, and plastics, and can establish the connection between the structure of materials and their bonds, as well as the resulting material properties.
Students will be familiar with the basic principles of material properties and their testing methods. They can use this knowledge to pre-select materials for specific technical applications.

syllabus_topics: Atomic structure, bonding types, crystal structures and lattice defects
Material properties and material testing: Elastic and plastic behavior, tensile test, hardness test, notched bar impact test, creep, material fatigue, non-destructive testing (NDT), strength increase
Ferrous materials: Iron and steel technology, iron-carbon diagram, TTT diagrams, classification, designation, and application areas
Non-ferrous metals: Production, properties, and application areas of technical non-ferrous metals
Glasses and Ceramics: Production and structure, classification and application areas
Polymers: Classification, properties, production and structure (bonding types, glass transition, etc.), technical polymers and application areas
assessment_rules: The graded examination is a written exam. The duration and scope of the exam are as specified in the currently valid study regulations.
